key_insight: Leaderboard scores for coding-agent performance optimization can be misleading because benchmark validity, runtime noise, and scoring rules can substantially change the apparent ranking.
engineering_relevance: For teams evaluating code-optimization agents, this study shows that benchmark results should be audited task-by-task before being used to claim progress or choose a model.
method: Replayed official reference patches for 740 optimization tasks across four Google Cloud machine types.
Checked whether replayed patches still satisfied each benchmark’s validity rules.
Compared public-submission rankings under different scoring rules and measured how often submissions matched or exceeded reference patches.
evidence_signal: Across cross-machine replays, only 39/102 GSO, 11/140 SWE-Perf, and 411/498 SWE-fficiency reference patches met the original validity rules everywhere, and 85.3% of replay-valid tasks had at least one public submission matching or beating the reference patch.
watch_item: Benchmark leaderboards may overweight unstable or weakly discriminative tasks, so reproducibility and per-task score weighting should be verified before trusting aggregate rankings.
paper_title: Are Performance-Optimization Benchmarks Reliably Measuring Coding Agents?
